title: Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Amendment Bill 2017
short_title: Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Amendment Bill 2017

divisions.question: The majority voted in favour of a motion introduced by Labor MP [Tony Burke](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/representatives/watson/tony_burke) (for Watson), but due to [confusion during the division](http://www.openaustralia.org.au/debates/?id=2017-08-15.88.2), the House [took this vote a second time](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/divisions/representatives/2017-08-15/6). ### Motion text > *That all words after "That" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > *"whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House notes that:* > *(1) the Government is failing to protect Australia's iconic Great Barrier Reef by:* >> *(a) failing to act on climate change;* >> *(b) supporting the Liberal National Party in Queensland in blocking reef protections aimed at halting the broad scale clearing of trees and remnant vegetation; and* >> *(c) winding back ocean protection, put in place by Labor, around Australia and specifically in the Coral Sea; and* > *(2) this Government cannot be trusted to protect the Great Barrier Reef and fight for Australia's unique environment."*
Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Amendment Bill 2017 - Second Reading - Speed things along

The majority voted against a motion introduced by Labor MP [Tony Burke](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/people/representatives/watson/tony_burke), which means it was unsuccessful. This is the [second time](https://theyvoteforyou.org.au/divisions/representatives/2017-08-15/4) that this same vote was taken. ### Motion text > *That all words after "That" be omitted with a view to substituting the following words:* > *"whilst not declining to give the bill a second reading, the House notes that:* > *(1) the Government is failing to protect Australia's iconic Great Barrier Reef by:* >> *(a) failing to act on climate change;* >> *(b) supporting the Liberal National Party in Queensland in blocking reef protections aimed at halting the broad scale clearing of trees and remnant vegetation; and* >> *(c) winding back ocean protection, put in place by Labor, around Australia and specifically in the Coral Sea; and* > *(2) this Government cannot be trusted to protect the Great Barrier Reef and fight for Australia's unique environment."*
Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Amendment Bill 2017 - Second Reading - Stop Adani mine

speeches.speaker: Tony Burke
speeches.brief: The speaker argued the bill fixes an unintended consequence where sunsetting regulations would automatically revoke Great Barrier Reef management plans, but criticised the government for failing to protect the reef by not acting on climate change, blocking land-clearing protections in Queensland, and winding back ocean protections including in the Coral Sea—the largest removal of ocean conservation areas in the world.

speeches.speaker: Craig Kelly
speeches.brief: The speaker argued that media reports about the 2016 Great Barrier Reef bleaching event were exaggerated and misleading, claiming only seven percent of the entire reef was bleached and 97 percent of tourism areas were unaffected. The speaker also highlighted the coalition government's $2 billion Reef 2050 Plan and criticised Labor's past record on reef management.

speeches.speaker: Jane Prentice
speeches.brief: The speaker argued in support of the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Amendment Bill 2017 to prevent management plans from being revoked when regulations sunset, and highlighted the coalition government's record on reef protection, including a $2 billion funding commitment, banning capital dredge disposal, and expanding the marine park to 344,400 square kilometres.

speeches.speaker: Joanne Ryan
speeches.brief: The speech supported the Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Amendment Bill 2017 to fix a sunset clause that would otherwise repeal management plans without replacement, and criticised the government's proposed marine park changes that would reduce fully protected green zones from 36% to 20% and double fishing zones. The speaker also outlined Labor’s alternative $100 million reef plan and climate change action, noting that at least $226 billion in assets could be exposed to inundation under rising sea levels.

speeches.speaker: Anthony Albanese
speeches.brief: The Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Amendment Bill was supported for its technical changes to prevent automatic revocation of management plans, while the coalition was criticised for climate inaction, rising emissions, and ocean protection rollbacks. Labor proposed a $100 million investment to improve reef management, a doubling of Indigenous rangers, and highlighted the reef's $56 billion economic value and 64,000 jobs.

speeches.speaker: Mark Butler
speeches.brief: Labor argued that climate change is the most serious threat to the Great Barrier Reef, noting carbon pollution fell 10% under the previous Labor government but has since risen under the current government. The speaker invited the Greens to amend their amendment to oppose taxpayer subsidies for the Adani Carmichael coalmine railway, indicating Labor would support that change.

speeches.speaker: Keith Pitt
speeches.brief: The Great Barrier Reef Marine Park Amendment Bill 2017 prevents plans of management from being automatically revoked if regulations are repealed, particularly through the sunset process, ensuring continued protective measures for the reef.
